## 2026-10-09 snapshot-scoped identity decisions (#21, still open)

Writes are idempotent by request key, compare the expected snapshot decision head inside an immediate transaction, validate that both entities belong to the workspace and snapshot and have matching types, and compare current name/type/exact-evidence fingerprints. Undo adds a new event. Alias components are transitive; attempts to create a distinct pair already connected by aliases, or alias components that violate an active distinct pair, return conflict. ## 2026-10-11 — P6 cast IDs separated from story evidence citations

The prior crop resolver still ordered references using `evidence_record_ids`, even though crops are keyed by character IDs. That made ordinary source-event citations fail to retrieve the correct crop. Screenplay generation now asks for `character_record_ids` separately, validates them against the frozen graph's canonical character entities, persists them per shot, and preserves existing targets when older UI payloads omit the field during an edit. Clip plans freeze both fields separately. The resolver now selects and orders crops by `target_character_ids`; the identity-review queue likewise prefers those cast IDs and only uses the narrowly validated legacy fallback when an old evidence ID exactly matches a graph character entity.

When a later scene is reached, an available verified crop for its first shot's target characters changes that scene's first prompt/clip to R2V; otherwise it retains the T2V route unless a selected style video requires R2V. A changed route triggers workflow-aware prompt preparation with the old prompt as visual-intent context. The frozen plan marks whether character refs are required, and admission/retry rebuilds and hash-checks the same refs. This fixes the data-model mismatch; it does not establish recognition accuracy or live visual coherence.
